chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Friday has a right and a sanctity; beware of neglecting or falling short in anything from the worship of Allah, the Exalted, and drawing near to Him through righteous deeds and abandoning all prohibitions. Indeed, Allah multiplies the good deeds in it, erases the bad deeds in it, and raises the ranks in it.
He said and mentioned that its day is like its night.

So if you are able to animate it with prayer and supplication, then do so. Indeed, your Lord descends from the beginning of the night of Friday to the lowest heaven, multiplying the good deeds in it and erasing the bad deeds in it. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, Generous.
ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and recommended acts of worship for Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah) is viewed as a microcosm of the Day of Judgment, a concept reinforced by the hadith's assertion that its day equals its night in spiritual merit. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the divine descent (Nuzul) to the lowest heaven as a unique opportunity for forgiveness, urging believers to actively 'animate' the day through sustained worship and adherence to the 'rights' of the day, which include both ritual acts and moral conduct.
